summary: Documented M2-S01 (access, tested by step-tester at envelopes/M2-S01/2026-09-18T15-29-25Z.json). Re-rendered PLAN.md and CLARIFICATIONS.md from plan.json (both had drifted since the builder, tester and an operator amendment wrote plan.json). Appended four open items to decisions.md (O-M2S01-01, O-M2S01-03, O-M2S01-04 open; O-M2S01-02 recorded CLOSED with the operator's prose-only amendment as the closing evidence) — no D- entries, because nothing in the builder's envelope met Step 3's technology-choice / design-trade-off / skill-gap / deviation bar beyond what the four open items already carry. Minted REQ-011 and REQ-012 and wrote workbook/03-profiles-permission-sets-and-psgs.md (Section 3 — Profiles + Permission Sets + PSGs, per this step's `access` type), two rows (CWB-PERM-001 the CustomPermission, CWB-PERM-002 the PermissionSet), owner named as the Sales Operations lead from Q13/the artefact's own description rather than the generic filler earlier sections used. Added two matching rows to traceability.md plus additive test-id-key and coverage paragraphs (no existing row or paragraph touched). Ran both named checkers and recorded their exit codes honestly: check_rtm.py exits 1 on a pre-existing REQ-010 coverage-gap ERROR unrelated to this step, plus 16 WARNs (14 pre-existing, 2 new from REQ-011/REQ-012's non-build-plan-shape `source` cells, the same class every prior row already carries); check_workbook.py on the per-step Section 3 slice exits 1 on nine structural 'Missing canonical section' ERRORs — a per-step slice necessarily carries one of ten sections, and Section 1's pre-existing slice produces the identical nine-error shape when linted the same way — with zero row-level findings. Moved M2-S01 tested -> documented via build_plan.py set-status.
confidence_rationale: Both addressable artefacts (the CustomPermission and the PermissionSet) produced a workbook row, each carrying a real source_req_id (REQ-011, REQ-012) minted from the step's own answered clarifications, an exactly-one recommended_agent, and a verification step stated in notes (the declared checker, xml, manifest results, and the one manual test named and deferred to the M2 gate rather than left blank). Both requirements the step serves have a traceability row. This is M2-S01's first documenting pass, so idempotence (no duplicate rows) is not yet exercised, but the row-keying (row_id for the workbook, req_id+step_id for traceability) is in place per Step 8 for the next pass to verify against. No artefact fell through to the Other configuration default; the step's `access` type routed cleanly to Section 3 per AGENT.md Step 4's table.

process_observations.observation: The builder's own extensions.open_items_for_the_human[] array (four entries, envelopes/M2-S01/2026-09-18T15-16-34Z.json) mapped 1:1 onto decisions.md's four new O- entries with no invented content and no gap on either side.

Neither new workbook row nor either new traceability row required a placeholder status, an inferred agent, or a fallback skill citation — every field traces to plan.json, the envelope, or the artefact files themselves.

The builder's own decision_record[11] ("which licence?") calls omitting <license> a 'documented skill default', while artefacts/M2-S01/deploy-order.md section 6 calls the same omission 'Recorded as an ambiguity, not a default' for the identical element. Neither text is this step's to edit (deploy-order.md is a read-only artefact per Step 1, and decision_record is the builder's own prior envelope), and the builder's own open_items_for_the_human[] table did not list this as a fifth open item, so this pass did not mint one either -- named here so a human deciding whether the four open items are the complete list has the discrepancy in view.

Two divergences from templates/admin/validation-rule-patterns.md's bypass contract -- the API name form (Bypass_Opportunity_Sales_Validation vs the template's Bypass_Validation_<Domain>) and the omission of the template's Integration_Bypass__c custom setting half -- are self-described by the builder as 'recorded, not corrected' and 'a deliberate half of a contract' respectively, but neither reached the builder's own numbered open-items table. This pass did not promote either to a decisions.md entry, since Step 3 only appends what the envelope records as one of its four kinds and the task's own brief scoped this pass to the four items the builder did number.

Whether the license-description inconsistency and the two template divergences above deserve their own O-M2S01-05/06/07 entries is a judgment call this pass left to a human -- the builder itself did not number them as open items, and inventing new ones this pass was not asked to open would be manufacturing a decision rather than recording one.
